o1.biggest_strength: Every concept is tied to a real review theme or buyer group, with the quiet-wheels gap and the cheaper women 25 to 40 audience both given their own ad and put in the top three.
o1.biggest_mistake: The test budget of about ₹7,700 per ad set buys roughly five purchases, nowhere near enough to separate ₹1,058 from ₹1,615, and there is no read split by gender, so the women-first bet cannot actually be proved.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Size each cell to a read you can trust and specify a gender and age breakdown plus a store-order reconciliation before any scale or cut decision.

o2.biggest_strength: The opening read is sharper than the brief: women 25 to 40 take 18% of spend but 26% of purchases, and the ₹292-a-trip reframe is a genuinely different angle on the ₹6,999 objection.
o2.biggest_mistake: The rollout is not fundable as written: three cells under broad targeting with a ₹4,500 floor buys about three purchases each, so no concept can be judged, and it contradicts its own women-only concept while also spending on the ₹2,188 41-plus group.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Give each concept its own audience and enough budget and a stated decision rule to produce a readable cost per purchase, and say what to stop instead of spreading to every group.

reason: Output 1 is the one I could hand to the team tomorrow: character-counted headlines, safe zones, light-colour shoot rules, a control cell, money thresholds for keep or cut, and a clear 'leave out 41 and over'. Output 2 opens with a better read of my numbers and has one idea I had not thought of, but its test plan would burn budget and prove nothing.
